analysis:
Examined all supplied patches, source and metadata against the canonical index and selected T-041 detail. Changes primarily affect serving availability (A-018, TB-002/TB-007, T-029) and residency coordination with the add-on hold (TB-012/T-059). No concrete regression is established in this scope.
ProviderLoop+Autopilot.swift:213 records a selected victim only after successful unload; command ownership, cancellation, lease checks and terminal capacity reporting remain visible. ProviderLoop+AutopilotBusy.swift:22 adds a recovery attempt to the busy gate rather than weakening exclusion. ProviderLoop+AutopilotControl.swift:76 refreshes saved selection from local configuration, without directly changing consent or serving authorization. The new SelectedModelPlacementPolicy.swift:25-33 gates release on protection, valid adoption, no hold and serving-only exclusions, then computes a deadline respecting delay, dwell and lease. Lines 41-48 withdraw adoption and report capacity without explicitly cancelling existing requests. No changes to keys, attestation, encryption, billing or T-041 cache scope/storage controls are visible.
Integration must inspect the new recovery mechanism and its state: noteSelectedModelUnloaded, selectedModelRecovery.attempt lifecycle, savedEnabledModels consumers, and checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue (ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift:82). Verify recovery respects shutdown, drain/add-on hold, command ownership and resource admission; deadline checks and selected/pinned protection precede release; withdrawal actually blocks new admission while allowing in-flight completion. Also trace releaseAdoptionForSelectedModelRecovery's capacity update (line 47) against the new capacity recovery callback for re-entry, and ensure attempt state clears on failure/cancellation. These implementations and callers are outside this batch, so neither a missing control nor their correctness is established. Determine whether the combined recovery policy needs availability-model documentation.
